summary: Chevening Scholarships are the UK government's international scholarship scheme, supported by the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO) and partner organisations. They let emerging leaders from Chevening-eligible countries and territories study a one-year taught master's degree at a UK university. Applicants need at least two years (2,800 hours) of work experience, a degree that qualifies them for a UK master's, and must choose three eligible UK courses. Chevening describes the benefit as a set of separate components: tuition fees, a monthly stipend, travel and several allowances.
eligibility_notes:
You must be a citizen of a Chevening-eligible country or territory. The country selector on the Chevening apply page shows which awards are open for each country; standard, SIDS and ASEAN awards have their own participating-country pages. For awards from an ODA-eligible country you must live in an ODA-eligible country and show a clear intention to support your country of award. People from European overseas territories may apply through the scheme of the European country they are citizens of.

You must not live in the UK when you apply (residents of British Overseas Territories are not excluded by this rule). You must commit to return to your country of award for at least two years after the scholarship ends.

You need at least two years (2,800 hours) of work experience gained after your undergraduate degree. You need an undergraduate degree that qualifies you for a UK master's, and you must have finished your undergraduate studies at least two years before the application deadline, even if you do not yet hold the certificate (you must have it by your interview). You must apply to three different eligible UK courses and hold at least one unconditional offer by the offer deadline on the timeline.

Chevening has no English language test requirement of its own (it was removed in 2020). You must still meet each university's own English requirements to get an unconditional offer.

Not eligible: holders of British or dual British citizenship (exceptions: citizens of a British Overseas Territory, and BN(O) holders applying from Hong Kong); people with refugee status in a country that is not eligible (a citizen of an eligible country with refugee status in another eligible country can apply); people who are, or in the last two years before applications opened were, employees of a government department, the British Council, a partner UK university or their wholly owned subsidiaries; immediate relatives of such employees (parents, step-parents, siblings, step-siblings, children, step-children, spouse, civil partner, long-term unmarried partner of 2+ years); people contracted to work on a British Council programme or project, and their relatives; and people who previously studied in the UK on a UK-government-funded scholarship. Former Chevening Fellows may apply only five years after completing the fellowship.

Having a master's degree already does not stop you applying for a second UK master's. Gender, age, sexual orientation, religion, marriage or parenthood status, caste and class do not matter for eligibility.
age_experience_notes: There is no upper age limit. Work experience: at least 2,800 hours after the undergraduate degree, spread over at least two years (the page describes this as roughly two years of full-time work at 35 hours a week). Full-time, part-time, voluntary work and paid or unpaid internships all count. Up to fifteen employment periods can be entered; the system multiplies weeks by hours per week for each entry. For the current cycle the undergraduate degree must have been completed by October 2024. You do not need to resign to apply, but you are responsible for making sure your employer will release you if you are selected. Applications without the required work experience are rejected.
funding_summary: The award is made up of separate components: payment of tuition fees, economy travel to and from your country of residence for the scholar only, an arrival allowance, the cost of the visa application for the scholar only, a departure allowance, up to GBP 75 towards a TB test where one is needed, a travel top-up allowance for events in London (only for those on non-London stipends) and a monthly living stipend. The stipend rate depends on studying inside or outside London and is reviewed each year; the pages give no figures. A scholarship lasts 12 months at most, and ends sooner if the course is shorter or the university withdraws visa sponsorship. Extensions are rare and cannot go beyond three extra months for a dissertation. There is no support for dependants.
programmes_note: Courses must be taught master's degrees that are full-time, based in the UK, start in the autumn term (usually September or October) and last between nine and twelve months. Not eligible: part-time or distance learning, research-focused MRes, PhD or DPhil, courses with more than one month of study outside the UK, and courses starting in January. The only diploma allowed is the postgraduate diploma in Diplomatic Studies at Oxford. London campuses are allowed only if the exact course is not offered at the main campus. Chevening does not publish a subject list; use its course finder, which shows only eligible courses. You rank three course choices, either similar courses at three universities or different courses at one university.
institutions_note: Any UK university with an eligible course can be chosen. Choosing a Chevening partner university does not change the funding, but the page says it may improve chances because fewer applicants compete for partner awards. Most universities contribute 20% towards tuition for Chevening scholars; if your chosen university does not, you may be asked to take another course or pay the difference. You may not transfer to another institution after the award.

summary.detail: One-year (9 to 12 months) full-time taught master's at a UK university starting in the autumn term. No Chevening subject list; any eligible course in the Chevening course finder. For MBA courses Chevening's contribution to tuition is capped at GBP 22,000 and universities may contribute up to 20% of the cap; the scholar pays the difference. Fees of other eligible courses are fully covered.
summary.source_text: Courses must be full-time, UK-based, taught master's

benefits.conditions: MBA: Chevening's contribution is capped at GBP 22,000 (universities may add up to 20% of the cap) and the scholar pays the difference. A part award covers either tuition only or stipend and allowances only. Resits and resubmitted work are not paid for.

benefits.limit_text: Monthly personal living allowance (stipend) for accommodation and living costs; amount not stated on the pages read
benefits.conditions: Rate depends on studying inside or outside London and is reviewed annually. Paid by the end of the month for the following full month and adjusted if the course starts or ends part-way through a month. Paid only for the length of the course. The final stipend is prorated to the earlier of the course end date or UK departure date. Suspended while abroad for more than 30 days in total.

benefits.limit_text: Economy return flight between country of residence and the UK by an approved route, for the scholar only
benefits.conditions: Must follow the Chevening travel policy and be booked through the nominated travel agent by the deadline given. Stopovers are not approved and dependants' travel is not covered. The flight home must leave at least one week before the visa end date.

benefits.limit_text: Arrival allowance paid once the scholar has arrived in the UK (amount not stated)
Departure allowance paid once the scholar has arranged to leave the UK at the end of the award (amount not stated)
Cost of the entry clearance (visa) application, for the scholar only
benefits.conditions: Do not apply for the visa before receiving the Final Award Letter. If there is no visa application centre in your country, travel to another country may be partly reimbursed after arrival in the UK.

benefits.limit_text: Up to GBP 75 contribution to a TB test
benefits.conditions: Only where a TB test is needed for the visa application.

benefits.limit_text: Travel top-up allowance to attend events in London (amount not stated)
benefits.conditions: Only for scholars who receive a non-London stipend.

benefits.limit_text: No insurance is listed among the benefits
benefits.conditions: The terms advise scholars to take out their own insurance for travel and stay in the UK.

benefits.limit_text: Dependants: no funding, support, visa endorsement or travel
benefits.conditions: The terms advise scholars not to bring dependants to the UK.

requirements.text: Online application with four essays written in English by you (AI-generated answers are prohibited): leadership and influencing, building professional relationships, course and university choice linked to UK priority areas, and career plan and long-term impact. No documents are uploaded at this stage.

Work history (up to 15 entries) totalling at least 2,800 hours, education history (up to 15 entries), and your top three UK master's courses chosen from the course finder, entered in the online application.

Two referees named in the application (two professional, two academic, or one of each; not a friend or relative). Letters are needed only if you are invited to interview, uploaded at least seven working days before the interview. In English, or in the original plus a notarised English translation in one file. Addressed to the British embassy or high commission in your country (or 'Chevening Officer' plus the country name if it has suspended operations). Each letter gives the referee's address, email and phone, how long and in what capacity they have known you, and when they last had regular contact with you, plus a short endorsement of leadership, networking, personal qualities and ability to complete a demanding UK programme.
requirements.conditional_rule: Only for applicants invited to interview

requirements.text: Passport or national ID card, uploaded at least seven days before the interview and shown in original at the interview, to verify identity and citizenship.
requirements.conditional_rule: Only for applicants invited to interview

requirements.text: Undergraduate certificate or diploma uploaded before the interview (transcripts are not accepted).
requirements.conditional_rule: Only for applicants invited to interview

requirements.text: At least one unconditional offer from one of your three UK courses, uploaded by the offer deadline. Pre-sessional English courses cannot be used to meet a university's English requirement.
requirements.conditional_rule: Only for applicants selected after interview

requirements.text: Conditional award task list: accept the award and its terms, upload offers from UK courses, upload passport details, and complete the health and disability disclosure form.
No Chevening English test. Each UK university sets its own English test and score for its application.

application_steps.title: Choose your country page and check you are eligible
application_steps.detail: Read the application guidance, then select your country or territory and the Scholarship option on the Chevening apply page. Applying is free and paper forms are not accepted. Chevening does not work with third parties who charge for application help.

application_steps.title: Register and pass the online eligibility checker
application_steps.detail: Accept the terms, register your email and mobile number, then answer the eligibility questions; you see the result immediately. The system gives you a unique access code that you need every time you return, so keep it safe. You are logged out after 15 minutes of inactivity.

application_steps.title: Complete every section and submit before closing
application_steps.detail: Fill in personal and immigration details, education history, work history (2,800 hours), your top three UK master's courses, two referees' contact details, four essays and the equal opportunities form. Then consent to the conditions and click submit and confirm. The timeline says applications close in October 2026 at 11:00 UTC (exact date on your country page). You cannot change an application after submitting.

application_steps.title: Eligibility check and reading committee
application_steps.detail: From October 2026 applications are checked against the eligibility criteria. Independent reading committees then assess eligible applications from mid-October 2026 to January 2027 on leadership and influencing, building professional relationships, course choice and UK priority areas, and career plan. Applicants must also show they have researched all three courses.

application_steps.title: Interview invitation and document upload
application_steps.detail: British embassies and high commissions shortlist candidates in mid-February 2027. Book your slot in the online system, then upload photo ID, your undergraduate certificate or diploma and two reference letters at least seven working days before the interview. Missing the reference deadline ends your application.

application_steps.title: Competency-based panel interview
application_steps.detail: Interviews run in March and April 2027 as a panel in English that includes embassy or high commission staff. Questions cover your application, aspirations, how Chevening helps your impact goals, your three courses and the status of your UK university applications. Bring your original photo ID.

application_steps.title: Result and conditional selection
application_steps.detail: Results are emailed from mid-June 2027 and dates vary by country. Candidates can be conditionally selected, placed on a reserve list, or unsuccessful. Reserve candidates can be upgraded only if they hold an unconditional offer. Chevening gives no feedback on applications or interviews and asks you not to contact the embassy about status.

application_steps.title: Secure an unconditional offer and accept the award
application_steps.detail: You apply directly to your three UK universities (statement, English test results, transcripts, references; deadlines vary and some courses close when full). Upload at least one unconditional offer by 17:00 BST on 8 July 2027 and complete the conditional award task list. The Final Award Letter is issued after the process is done and your university confirms your place.

application_steps.title: Apply for the visa and travel to the UK
application_steps.detail: Do not apply for your visa until you have the Final Award Letter. Studies start in September or October 2027. You must attend the Chevening Orientation event at the start and the Farewell event at the end (a GBP 100 penalty applies for missing a mandatory event without a listed reason).

application_steps.title: Follow the award conditions during the year
application_steps.detail: Study the agreed course and pass at the first attempt. Stay in the UK except for authorised absences, with no more than 30 days outside the UK in total. You may work part-time within Home Office and university rules (no more than 20 hours a week in term time and 40 in vacations). Return all surveys and reports and keep the Secretariat informed of contact details and changes. Deferral is granted only for pregnancy.

application_steps.title: Return home for at least two years
application_steps.detail: Book your flight home through the nominated travel agent by the deadline given. You must return to your home country for at least two years after the scholarship, tell the British embassy or high commission when you are back, and not switch or extend your visa. Failing the two-year residence is a breach and you may have to repay everything paid. A third country may be allowed only in exceptional cases where returning is impossible because of conflict.
